questions.stem: Given the inequality chain Z = T ≤ P ≥ S > U, decide which conclusions follow. I: P ≥ U. II: S ≥ U.
options: Both conclusions I and II follow
Either conclusion I or II follows
questions.explanation: Exhaustive valid-order checking confirms: I is always true and II is always true.

questions.stem: Given the inequality chain S = P ≤ T > W > X, decide which conclusions follow. I: S > P. II: W = X.
options: Both conclusions I and II follow
Either conclusion I or II follows
questions.explanation: Exhaustive valid-order checking confirms: I is not necessarily true and II is not necessarily true.

questions.stem: Given the inequality chain S > Q < V > X > P, decide which conclusions follow. I: V > X. II: Q > X.
options: Both conclusions I and II follow
Either conclusion I or II follows
questions.explanation: Exhaustive valid-order checking confirms: I is always true and II is not necessarily true.

questions.stem: Given the inequality chain S > R > Z > X ≥ T, decide which conclusions follow. I: S < X. II: Z = X.
options: Both conclusions I and II follow
Either conclusion I or II follows
questions.explanation: Exhaustive valid-order checking confirms: I is not necessarily true and II is not necessarily true.

questions.stem: Given the inequality chain U < R ≤ V > X > P, decide which conclusions follow. I: X = P. II: U ≤ R.
options: Both conclusions I and II follow
Either conclusion I or II follows
questions.explanation: Exhaustive valid-order checking confirms: I is not necessarily true and II is always true.

questions.stem: Statements: No dancers are sailors. Some sailors are runners. Conclusions: I. Some runners are not dancers. II. No runners are dancers. Which conclusion follows?
options: Both conclusions I and II follow
Either conclusion I or II follows
questions.explanation: The B∩C members are outside A; other C members remain unrestricted.

questions.stem: Statements: All artists are sailors. No sailors are singers. Conclusions: I. No artists are singers. II. Some artists are singers. Which conclusion follows?
options: Both conclusions I and II follow
Either conclusion I or II follows
questions.explanation: A is contained in B, while B and C are disjoint.

questions.stem: Statements: Some poets are sailors. No sailors are drivers. Conclusions: I. Some poets are not drivers. II. All poets are drivers. Which conclusion follows?
options: Both conclusions I and II follow
Either conclusion I or II follows
questions.explanation: The A∩B members cannot be C.

questions.stem: Statements: Some pilots are bakers. Some bakers are drivers. Conclusions: I. Some pilots are drivers. II. Some bakers are pilots. Which conclusion follows?
options: Both conclusions I and II follow
Either conclusion I or II follows
questions.explanation: The two Some overlaps need not coincide; Some A are B converts to Some B are A.

questions.stem: Statements: All bakers are artists. Some teachers are bakers. Conclusions: I. Some teachers are artists. II. Some artists are teachers. Which conclusion follows?
options: Both conclusions I and II follow
Either conclusion I or II follows
questions.explanation: The existing C∩A members must lie in B, proving both conclusions.
